title: His eyes were red when his father
html_source: As Molly is thinking about sex with a priest and reminiscing about Boylan, there are two lines that seem to refer to Bloom’s grief over his father’s death: ‘his eyes were red when his father died’ and a few lines later ‘I suppose he was thinking of his father’; however, Rudolph died in 1886 when Bloom was 18, two years before he began courting Molly; this implies that they had known each other for at least a couple of years before becoming romantically involved. The first line follows Molly’s wondering if her confessor recognizes her in the confessional. The second line occurs in the midst of Molly’s recollection of her and Boylan’s post-coital snack and slumber. The alternative explanation for these lines–i.e., that the first reference is to Fr Corrigan’s father and the second is to Boylan’s father–seem totally implausible.
